Necromancer · Meta

Blood Wave Necromancer

one-button blood caster

Necromancer meta unchanged one-button blood caster

Last verified 2026-08-09 • Season 14

Move on whenKessime's Legacy equipped. The guide's own line is 'once you get a good Kessime's Legacy, the true power of the build will be revealed' - before it you cast one wave, after it you cast two and the build pulls monsters into them for you.
Move on whenRing of Starless Skies crafted. The guide names it the top crafting priority because 'it will solve most of your resource issues, and increase your damage' - and the Resource Cost Reduction requirement drops from over 25% to over 15% the moment it lands.
Move on whenRing of Starless Skies, Banished Lord's Talisman and Red Blessing all online, and you are ready to rebuild the character around 100% block chance and Resolve stacking - which is a different gear set, not a different rotation.

Skill bar

1Reap
2Blood Wave
3Blood Lance
4Sever
5Bone Prison
6Blood Mist

Rotation

Sever to teleport onto a pack, which also drops a corpse; Blood Mist eats that corpse for the Flesh Eater legendary node and teleports you again. Blood Lance from range to dump Overpower stacks, then hold Blood Wave to regain them - you have to spend before you can gain when you are at capacity. Bone Prison on anything that survives, for the attack speed. Weave Reap when Essence runs dry.

Skill point priority

  1. Honest scope note: this is an endgame-only guide. It says outright 'this build guide assumes you have a Level 70 Character and unlocked Torment 1' and defers levelling to Maxroll's separate Necromancer levelling guides, so this stage records the guide's own Starter variant - a level-70, Torment-1 entry point - rather than a 1-70 route nobody published
  2. Blood Wave to max first: it is the only damage skill and the entire rotation
  3. Take Hematolagnia, the key passive that turns Blood Wave into a Core skill with no cooldown, the moment it is available - the build does not exist without it
  4. Blood Lance next, purely as the Overpower-stack spender that re-triggers Bloodbath
  5. Bone Prison for attack speed; the guide leans on it hard ('you get a lot of Cap 2 attack speed from Bone Prison in this build')
  6. Sever, Blood Mist and Reap at one point each - mobility, corpse generation and an Essence patch, not damage

Skill bar

1Reap
2Blood Wave
3Blood Lance
4Sever
5Bone Prison
6Blood Mist

Rotation

The same loop, but most of it is now automatic. Curses run themselves: the Wat rune applies Decrepify, Life Tap generates Blood Orbs, and the Teb rune spends them on Iron Maiden, which is what applies Vulnerable. So you rotate Sever and Blood Mist for movement as Blood Mist comes off cooldown, and otherwise hold Blood Wave. Bone Prison on anything tanky - the guide notes Blood Wave 'one shots most t12 stuff' but that Bone Prison 'increases your DPS significantly' on the rest.

Skill point priority

  1. Blood Wave and Hematolagnia maxed - unchanged, everything else is support
  2. Blood Lance kept only for the Bloodbath and Overpower-spend loop
  3. Bone Prison maxed: the attack-speed engine the guide keeps citing
  4. Sever and Blood Mist stay at one point - teleport, Unstoppable, and corpse consumption for Flesh Eater
  5. Reap stays at one point; its job shrinks as Essence regeneration comes online
  6. Stat gates the guide sets for this stage: over 15 Essence Regeneration, over 25% Resource Cost Reduction, three greater-affix 'Lucky Hit: Chance to Restore Resource' tempers on jewelry, over 60% Critical Strike Chance and over 50% attack speed with Ferocity stacks

Skill bar

1Reap
2Blood Wave
3Blood Lance
4Sever

Rotation

Identical to the early endgame - Sever and Blood Mist to move, Blood Lance to dump Overpower, Blood Wave held down, Bone Prison on cooldown for tanky targets. What changes here is the gear, not the gameplay: this is where the Aspect swap onto boots and the amulet transfiguration land.

Skill point priority

  1. Blood Wave and Hematolagnia maxed
  2. Bone Prison maxed for the attack-speed cap
  3. Blood Lance held at the rank that keeps the Overpower loop turning
  4. Stat gates: over 15 Essence Regeneration, over 15% Resource Cost Reduction now that Starless Skies carries it, three greater-affix Lucky Hit restore tempers on jewelry, over 70% Critical Strike Chance, over 50% attack speed
  5. Survivability is the remaining problem, and the guide's answer is Embattled Aspect plus Endurant Faith - noting openly that the instant fortify healing this relies on is a bug

Skill bar

1Reap

6Blood Mist

Rotation

Read the guide's warning first, because it is the difference between a run and a death: 'Decrepify is how you generate Resolve stacks via Resolve modifier. But when you start your pit/tower run, you have no stacks. If you engage big packs you will insta die.' So open on a small pull, cast Blood Wave until Resolve reaches roughly 10 stacks, and only then push the floor. Steady state: Blood Lance from range before every pack for Bloodbath's second half and Disobedience's damage reduction, Bone Prison before the pack reaches you, Corpse Tendrils for Vulnerable and Flesh Eater, Blood Mist every eight seconds, Blood Wave held down throughout - Overpower stays pinned at 11 on its own once it is running.

Skill point priority

  1. Sever comes off the bar for Corpse Tendrils, taken with the Jaws Of Death variant - the guide's reason is that it 'makes the cast instant and it consumes corpses which activates Flesh Eater paragon node to get 60%x damage multiplier'
  2. Bone Prison rises in priority: cast it on cooldown, it is both the attack-speed engine and physical cover
  3. Blood Lance now does double duty - Overpower spending and triggering Aspect of Disobedience for 45% damage reduction
  4. Blood Mist every eight seconds or so for Unstoppable and corpse consumption
  5. Reap becomes a corpse generator rather than an Essence patch
  6. Hard gate: 100% block chance, which is what activates Aspect of Redirected Force. Also two greater-affix Lucky Hit restore tempers on jewelry, over 70% Critical Strike Chance and at least 50% attack speed

How to run them

The guide publishes two pairings and switches between them. While you are still gearing it hires Aldkin, purely for the 15% Critical Strike Chance and the early sustain - 'getting critical strike chance to 100% is not as easy especially during the early game'. From the midgame on it hires Subo instead, for map visibility and a 25% Critical Damage multiplier, which is what the recorded tree above is. The Reinforcement never changes: Raheir on Bastion, 'great for survivability'. Icy Veins dissents and hires Varyana; Maxroll is the construction source here and its own author swaps mercenaries with progression, so the honest reading is that the hire is a tuning knob and Raheir/Bastion is the fixed part.

Uniques & where to find them

Kessime's Legacypants

The build's enabler and the first thing to chase. Target-farm Andariel, and gamble pants at the vendor in parallel - the guide's own instruction is 'Gamble pants to acquire Kessime's Legacy. They also drop from Andariel's.' The plain Unique is fine: the guide says the Mythic upgrade 'doesn't provide a significant benefit'.

Where →
Ring of Starless Skiesring 1

Mythic Unique, and the guide's crafting priority #1 because it solves the build's resource problem outright. Rare drop from any lair boss, or craft it in the Horadric Cube with Pandemonium Fragments - remembering that only one Cube-crafted Mythic can be equipped at a time.

Where →
Banished Lord's Talismanamulet

Mythic Unique, crafting priority #2 for the endgame variant. General Unique Pool - any lair boss can drop it - or Horadric Cube conversion. Interchangeable with Red Blessing between the amulet and the charm slot; the guide prefers this one on the amulet because 'Banished Lord's Talisman has better affixes'.

Where →
Blood-Mad Idolamulet

Mythic Unique, and the push variant only - it displaces Banished Lord's Talisman there. General Unique Pool or Horadric Cube. The guide is blunt about the trade: it 'makes surviving more of a challenge but damage gain is so significant that it is worth it', and it keeps Aspect of Untimely Death live because you are constantly losing and regaining Life.

Where →

Loot filter

maxroll.gg
Blood Wave Necromancer — Maxroll Light / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes)

The guide ships its own filters as import codes in its Loot Filter section rather than as a permalink, in three strictness tiers. These are the exact-match option. No Blood-Wave-specific filter exists on the community filter sites; the closest is https://diablo4lootfilter.com/filters/lancewave-necromancer-full-endgame-pit-135-d4-loot-filter, a LanceWave (Blood Lance / Blood Wave hybrid) endgame filter that shares Kessime's Legacy and the Blood affix pool but is not tuned to this build's Essence-regen and Lucky-Hit-restore priorities. Preview either before importing.

Summary

The Necromancer's carry build this season, and the most genuinely one-button build in the repo. Lord of Hatred's Hematolagnia key passive converts Blood Wave from an Ultimate into a Core skill - no cooldown, an Essence cost instead - and Kessime's Legacy then fires two waves per cast from both sides while pulling monsters in, so the old orb-pickup-and-reset gameplay is gone entirely. The multiplier engine is Overpower: you dump stacks with Blood Lance and regain them casting Blood Wave, which re-triggers the Bloodbath legendary node and the Dominate glyph. Cross-checked, and the sources genuinely disagree about how good that is: Maxroll's overall endgame list rates Blood Wave A, Maxroll's push list rates it A, Icy Veins rates it S, and TierListHQ's fresher 3.1.2 snapshot rates the class A with the comment that Blood Wave 'overperforms' but has 'limited depth behind it'. Two honest warnings. First, resource: the guide admits 'early on resource management can be an issue since Blood Wave as a core skill is very resource hungry', which is why the affix priorities below are dominated by Essence Regeneration and Resource Cost Reduction until Ring of Starless Skies lands. Second, and more serious, the endgame survivability package leans on a bug the guide states outright - 'Embattled Aspect makes your fortify healing instant (it is a bug)' - and pairs it with Endurant Faith so a finished character 'can feel quite immortal'. Treat that tech as volatile: it is the obvious patch target, and the build is still fine without it, just squishier. The guide author lists no cons beyond early gearing, which is worth reading as enthusiasm rather than as evidence.
